question: the Build phase concluded 'in a packed rewrite the share stops paying'. This measures the share's value in ALL THREE languages on the same model, to see whether that is a language finding or a property of the model's share.
reading: the model's cross-configuration share is worth 1.7% in Python, 4.1% in Rust and 7.0% in Go -- it never paid much in ANY language, so the model cannot support the claim that a rewrite is what made it stop paying. The real kernel's share value inside a cold six-config build is not measured anywhere (the cost model's 337.9 s cold figure already includes it, and its 194.9 s warm figure is the persisted trace STORE, a different mechanism).
